name: Yong Kwon Cho
title: Professor
department: Civil and Environmental Engineering; Institute for Robotics and Intelligent Machines
fitReason: Applied embodied-perception and HRI option: real robot sensing around moving workers, semantic tracking and socially aware navigation. Current local graduate supervision is established. A short perception/robustness evaluation project is a possible research fit, not an advertised master’s summer visit.

physicalEvidence.summary: The complete ICRA 2025 workshop paper deploys YOLOv8 at 10 Hz with upward-facing fisheye imagery, LiDAR SLAM and modified Kalman tracking on an actual quadruped. Two participants perform indoor bricklaying while the robot moves along a corridor using an autonomous navigation package; a 150-second sensor sequence and Vicon reference trajectories support evaluation. This paper evaluates perception, leaving use of tracked people for social navigation as future work. A separate journal extension, published online September 23, 2026, explicitly reports real-testbed navigation using sensor-fusion detections with social-force-augmented DWA. Its full methods were not accessible, so the exact detector/version and detailed navigation protocol are not presumed identical. This is learned perception coupled to conventional planning, not an end-to-end learned locomotion policy. The July 2026 arXiv upload of the workshop paper is not a new experiment.

shortVisit.summary: The live RICAL openings section welcomes visiting PhD students and recruits funded degree-seeking graduate research assistants. It does not explicitly invite visiting master’s students. Current/past visiting researchers and undergraduates on the roster do not establish a general external-master offer, funding or a summer 2027 slot.

unknowns: Use current official Professor title. Older RICAL biography has overlapping Associate/Professor date ranges, and a 2024 NUS visiting distinction does not establish a current non-US primary appointment.

The complete 2025 workshop experiment provides limited-duration indoor moving-platform perception evidence. The newer 2026 journal abstract establishes a navigation extension, but unavailable full methods limit precision about deployment and controller details.

The 2026 conference chapter on imitation-learning observation features explicitly uses Unity simulation. Do not substitute that chapter, unpublished GNN titles or older CrossLoco coauthorship for the documented recent local perception experiment.

Existing Georgia Tech institutional guidance allows a conditional outside undergraduate/graduate Student Intern route with continued enrollment, degree relevance, return to the home program and at least 32 hours per week. It does not broaden this lab’s PhD-scoped invitation.

Existing Georgia Tech funding guidance lists $1,800 per month and permits self- or department funding, but this is a financial-evidence minimum, not a total travel budget or 2027 guarantee. Host approval, exact dates, insurance, fees, remote option and mentor capacity remain unknown.
The journal issue is January 2027 but the work was already published online September 23, 2026. It is not treated as a future unobserved publication.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
